headline: Granted utility work on Bridge, Naples, Webb streets and Jefferson Ave; adopted October taxi pickup zones and $10,768.48 school salary payment.
summary: The council granted National Grid conduit requests and a GoNetSpeed fiber-optic request. It confirmed several appointments by 10-0-1 roll call votes, held others to the next meeting, and paid prior-year school, parking, and engineering invoices. It also adopted weekend taxi and rideshare pickup zones for October and received a Planning Board report on data center zoning.

ORDERED: The City Council hereby authorizes the Mayor to enter into a five-year 
contract with Via Transportation, Inc., doing business as River North Transit LLC of 
New York, New York for an on demand rideshare program. 
 
Discussion: 
 
Councillor Davis: This contract is for the Salem Skipper.  The City recently received a 
recent grant from MassDot which will enable the city to maintain the service until at 
least June 30, 2027.  The contract is for 5 years which allows for periodic extensions 
past that point subject to future funding. 
 
Councillor King: I am also thrilled to see this on here because it means extending the 
program through June of next year.  I will note that the City Council is voting tonight 
because the contract is being extended for five years, and that is why it is in front of 
us.  I would love to see the contract in the future cases when the whole point is the 
contract is why we're reviewing it.  I think this appended before where there is no 
contract in the back up.  would like to see the contract in the future. 
 
Councillor Holappa:  I have a mind to vote against this tonight, which might sound 
crazy if you've ever met me or heard me talk about transportation.  It's because of how 
little information the Council has around this.  We as as mentioned have not seen the 
contract, there is no information in the backup material that there's a notion to find 
more sustainable funding plan, as was mentioned by Councillor Davis there a grant 
that is going to extend this until next year, mid next year. I really would prefer to have

#469-RESOLUTION HONORING ILENE SIMONS - RETIRED CITY CLERK 
 
The following Resolution Honoring retired City Clerk Ilene Simons was adopted by a 
Roll Call Vote of 10-0-1.  Councillor Prrosniewski was recorded as absent. 
 
RESOLUTION HONORING ILENE SIMONS - Retired City Clerk 
 
WHEREAS, Ilene Simons has devoted more than twenty-five years of service to the City of 
Salem and its residents, including service as Assistant City Clerk and, since 2018, as City 
Clerk; and 
WHEREAS, throughout her career, Ilene has served the people of Salem with 
professionalism, integrity, patience, good humor, and an unwavering dedication to public 
service; and 
 WHEREAS, as City Clerk and Salem’s Chief Election Official, Ilene has overseen the fair, 
accurate, and orderly administration of our elections, faithfully safeguarding the 
democratic process and ensuring that Salem’s residents can exercise their most 
fundamental civic right with confidence; and 
 WHEREAS, Ilene has been a trusted partner, confidant, counselor, and mentor to 
countless City Councillors, providing guidance rooted in deep institutional knowledge, 
sound judgment, and an enduring respect for the responsibilities of public office; and 
WHEREAS, through decades of service at the center of municipal government, Ilene has 
become a steward of the City Council’s institutional memory and a guardian of Salem’s 
civic history, customs, and traditions, preserving the continuity of an institution that 
extends far beyond any individual elected official; and

WHEREAS, over those many years, Ilene has seen the full range of Salem’s famously 
engaged civic life, and has met it all with patience, steadiness, discretion, and good 
humor; and 
WHEREAS, her dedication to the City Council, City government, Salem’s residents, and 
the democratic institutions we share represents the very best of public service; 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Salem City Council, on behalf of the 
residents of the City of Salem, expresses its profound gratitude to Ilene Simons for her 
extraordinary service and for the wisdom, integrity, steadiness, and friendship she has 
brought to City Hall throughout her distinguished career; and 
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Salem City Council extends its warmest 
congratulations to Ilene upon her retirement and its sincere wishes for happiness and 
fulfillment in the years ahead.

Be it Ordained by the City Council of the City of Salem, as follows: 
Section 1. Chapter 24 – Offenses and Miscellaneous Provisions is hereby amended by 
adding 
a new section as follows: 
“Sect. 24-33 – Gas-Powered Leaf Blowers 
(a) Purpose 
The use of gasoline-powered leaf blowers contributes to noise pollution, air 
contamination, and the release of harmful particulate matter. This ordinance seeks to 
protect the public health, welfare, and the environment by limiting the use of gas-
powered leaf blowers, while also promoting the adoption of cleaner alternatives. 
(b) Definitions 
Commercial leaf blower operator: Any entity that receives income, remuneration, or 
compensation of any kind, whether as a fee, a charge, a salary, wages, or otherwise, for 
operating a leaf blower. All City Departments and their contractors are excluded from this 
definition. 
Gas-powered leaf blower: Any portable handheld or backpack style power device that is 
powered by a petroleum-based engine and used in any landscape maintenance, 
construction, property repair, or property maintenance for the purpose of blowing, 
moving, removing, dispensing, or redistributing leaves, dust, dirt, grass clippings, 
cuttings, and trimmings from trees and shrubs or any other type of litter or debris. 
Property Manager: Any tenant in possession or person or entity in control of real property, 
including, but not limited to, a condominium association. 
Property Owner: The legal owner of record of real property as listed by the tax assessor’s 
records.
